issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 125 of 165 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: The Castings category exhibits severe fragmentation with 125 suppliers accounting for only 20% (USD 4,440,995) of the USD 22,403,282 total spend, while the HHI of 764 indicates highly dispersed purchasing power. With the top supplier (Frontier United Components Pvt Ltd) holding only 21% share, the organization lacks leverage and incurs excessive administrative overhead across 165 suppliers for a single category.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct strategic sourcing event to consolidate the 125 tail suppliers (USD 4,440,995 spend) into 3-5 preferred Castings suppliers, targeting Frontier United Components Pvt Ltd and 2-4 additional strategic partners for expanded volume commitments
Negotiate volume-tiered pricing agreements with selected preferred suppliers, leveraging the consolidated USD 4,440,995 tail spend to secure 8-12% cost reduction and standardized payment terms
Implement supplier blocking for 100-110 tail suppliers representing minimal spend (<USD 20,000 each) across all ERPs and route demand to preferred suppliers via updated source lists
Establish quarterly business reviews with the 3-5 preferred suppliers to monitor performance, innovation, and continuous improvement initiatives
Deploy supplier scorecarding in Coupa for preferred Castings suppliers tracking quality, delivery, and cost KPIs to maintain competitive tension

plan.expected_impact: Consolidation of 125 tail suppliers into 3-5 preferred partners will reduce administrative costs and capture USD 355,000 to USD 533,000 in annual savings (8-12% of the USD 4,440,995 tail spend) through improved pricing leverage and reduced transaction overhead.
kpis: Active Castings supplier count reduction from 165 to 60 or fewer within 6 months
HHI improvement from 764 to 1,200+ indicating healthier concentration
Tail spend percentage reduction from 20% to below 10% of category spend
Cost savings achievement of USD 355,000-533,000 (8-12% of tail spend)
PO administrative cost reduction of 70-80% for tail supplier transactions
risks: Supply disruption risk during transition if tail suppliers are blocked before preferred suppliers confirm capacity for USD 4.4M additional volume
Preferred suppliers may lack technical capability for specialized castings currently sourced from niche tail suppliers
Increased concentration risk if consolidation reduces supplier base too aggressively without geographic or technology redundancy
Requisitioner resistance and maverick buying if tail supplier blocking lacks change management and communication
Multi-ERP environment complexity may cause incomplete blocking, allowing continued tail supplier usage in Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, or NetSuite
erp_actions: SAP: Set posting block flag in LFA1 and purchasing organization block in LFB1 for 100-110 tail suppliers below USD 20,000 annual spend
SAP: Create and enforce source lists (ME01) for Castings material groups designating 3-5 preferred suppliers with MRP-relevant flags
Oracle EBS: Set supplier sites to inactive status for blocked tail suppliers and update approved supplier lists (ASL) to restrict requisition creation
Dynamics 365: Update vendor accounts to 'On hold' status for blocked suppliers and configure purchasing policies to enforce preferred supplier routing
NetSuite: Apply 'Inactive' vendor status for tail suppliers and establish item-level preferred vendor records for Castings commodity codes
Coupa: Implement catalog punchouts or preferred supplier forms for the 3-5 strategic Castings partners and configure guided buying rules to steer requisitions
All ERPs: Negotiate and configure extended payment terms (Net 60-75) with preferred suppliers to offset any pricing premiums and improve working capital by estimated USD 300,000-400,000
